title: Generation 1 — c. 1672, under the Chand kings
description: Sukhdev's generation lived under the Chand dynasty, roughly a century after Almora became their capital in the 1560s. A rural hill homestead era — stone-and-wood houses, terraced subsistence farming, and temple-building at its height across Kumaon.

title: Generation 2 — c. 1699, Chand-era Kumaon
description: Still under Chand rule. The hand-block textile tradition that would later flourish — including the ceremonial pichhaura — was already taking root in the region.

title: Generation 3 — c. 1726, Chand-era Kumaon
description: The 18th century saw the pichhaura craft flourish across Kumaon, with trade routes bringing dyes and cloth into the hills.

title: Generation 4 — c. 1753, late Chand dynasty
description: The last decades of Chand rule, which had governed Kumaon from Almora since the 1560s and would end in 1790.

title: Generation 5 — c. 1780, the eve of change
description: Chand rule was ending. Within a decade, the Gorkha kingdom of Nepal would take control of Kumaon.

title: Generation 6 — c. 1807, under Gorkha rule
description: Kumaon was under Gorkha administration (1790–1815) — a period remembered in Kumaoni oral history as harsher than what came before or after.

title: Generation 7 — c. 1834, early British rule
description: The British East India Company had taken Kumaon from the Gorkhas in 1815, after the Anglo-Nepalese War. New roads, forestry rules, and colonial administration reached the hills.

title: Generation 8 — c. 1861, after 1857
description: Just years after the Indian Rebellion of 1857, in which Kumaonis — especially from Champawat, under Kalu Singh Mahara — rose against British rule.

title: Generation 9 — c. 1888, high British Raj
description: The British hill-station era in full swing nearby (Nainital, Ranikhet), though Almora itself — unlike those towns — was never built up by the British; it stayed a Kumaoni-shaped town.

title: Generation 10 — c. 1915, the First World War
description: Kumaoni men served in the World War as part of the British Indian Army — the same regiment whose marching song, Bedu Pako Baro Masa, is still sung today.

title: Generation 11 — c. 1942, war and the movement for independence
description: The year of the Quit India Movement, and of many Kumaonis joining the Indian National Army under Subhas Chandra Bose during the Second World War.

title: Generation 12 — c. 1969, independent India
description: Kumaon was now part of independent India, still within Uttar Pradesh state (Uttarakhand wouldn't be carved out until 2000). The era of migration for education and work — to Delhi, and far beyond — that this family's own records reflect.

title: Generation 13 — c. 1996, contemporary Kumaon
description: Uttarakhand became its own state in 2000. A generation with far greater reach — this family's own journeys map shows members who've travelled as far as Canada and Angola while Bairati remains home.

title: Generation 14 — c. 2023, today
description: The newest generation recorded in this tree.
